page: Vultr voc-g-32c-128gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance designed for multi-threaded and memory-intensive applications. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture supports standard x86 extensions including AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, though newer vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX are not present. Cache resources comprise 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations record exceptionally high memory throughput, with large-block uncached read speeds reaching 537.96 GB/sec and write speeds of 292.8 GB/sec, placing memory bandwidth in the top tier. Storage is bundled directly via a 640 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering rapid local block storage without reliance on network-attached volumes. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators, focusing purely on general compute density. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate strong multi-core computational throughput, reflected in elevated PassMark CPU scores, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rates of 209.38 GB/sec, and Clang compilation metrics. In database and caching benchmarks, the configuration achieves 73.66 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics, including single-threaded gzip compression and base Geekbench single-core results, place in the middle performance tier due to the 2.0 GHz clock speed profile.

This server offers high resource efficiency for horizontally parallelized workloads that benefit from dedicated core allocations and high memory bus capacity. It represents an effective technical fit for in-memory databases, Redis instances, continuous integration and build servers, medium-sized model inference generation, and multi-tenant application serving.
description: Vultr voc-g-32c-128gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor platform, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 128 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, coupled with a 640 GB local NVMe SSD. Hardware accelerators are omitted, with GPU count sitting at zero. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 537 GB/s for reads alongside strong multi-core processing performance, evidenced by robust Geekbench multi-core and Clang software compilation results. Single-threaded tasks and single-core metrics fall within average industry percentiles due to the conservative base frequency, and advanced vector extensions like AVX-512 are absent. Consequently, resource efficiency is highest in parallelized multi-threaded tasks. The configuration is well suited for enterprise database hosting, distributed caching via Redis, automated CI/CD build environments, and scalable web serving backends.
